page: Amazon Web Services g7.metal is a bare-metal server instance belonging to the Accelerated Computing family. It features 192 dedicated physical x86_64 cores running at 3.9 GHz without multi-threading, paired with 768 GB of system memory, providing a consistent ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The host configuration delivers direct, unvirtualized hardware access to the underlying Intel processor resources.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by an array of 8 NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 4500 GPUs, supplying an aggregate of 256 GB of GPU video memory. The platform integrates 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and establishes network throughput through a 700 Gbps baseline interface, catering to high-throughput data transfer requirements between the host system, disk arrays, and cluster environments.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, g7.metal consolidates substantial compute density, large local non-volatile storage, and dedicated multi-GPU capacity into a single bare-metal chassis. This dense footprint mitigates virtualization overhead and multi-instance interconnect latencies. The instance is suited for multi-GPU graphics rendering, computer vision, distributed model inference pipelines, and high-bandwidth engineering simulations.
description: Amazon Web Services g7.metal is an accelerated bare-metal instance designed for high-density graphics and parallel compute tasks. It runs on a dedicated 192-core Intel x86_64 architecture operating at 3.9 GHz with one thread per core, matched with 768 GB of system RAM. Hardware acceleration is powered by 8 NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 4500 GPUs offering 256 GB of combined VRAM. High-bandwidth operations are facilitated by 7600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 700 Gbps. Lacking virtualization overhead, this bare-metal host eliminates hypervisor contention while maximizing processing efficiency across substantial CPU and GPU allocations. The balanced compute density, massive localized NVMe capacity, and extensive network pipeline position the instance for demanding graphics virtualization, workstation streaming, visual computing, and large-scale parallel processing workloads.
